drhp.business: We operate an asset-light business, wherein Karigars hand craft jewellery according to Client’s requirement and act as principal contractor, managing the design, material sourcing, and finished Jewellery making process for our clients. We offer a diverse range of high-quality hand-crafted gold jewellery in 22-karat and 18-karat. It is essentially an asset-light model in which we offer our expertise in jewellery design, craftsmanship and timely delivery of our products to all our customers who are spread PAN India.
drhp.one_liner: We offer a diverse range of high-quality hand-crafted gold jewellery in 22-karat and 18-karat.
risks: Our business and the demand for our product is reliant on the success of our customers’ products with end consumers, and any decline in the demand for the end-products could have an adverse impact on our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.
Jewellers, particularly smaller players, need to maintain large gold inventories to meet customer demand.
Our customers, including Corporate Clients, further sell our products to end use customers.
For further details in relation to our customers, see “Our Business” on page 194.

Any material downturn in any of our customers services, as a result of increased competition, seasonality of demand, our customers’ failure to successfully market their products or to compete effectively, loss of market share, macroeconomic conditions in the markets of key end-customers, regulatory action, litigation, pricing fluctuation or other factors may impact us.

Any of these factors could have an adverse effect on the end-use customers and sales of our product could decline substantially which could adversely affect our profitability and result of operations.
Additionally, the prices of gold and diamonds at a particular time also affect the decision of our customers to purchase jewellery.
Most of our end-customers of our customers are individuals who purchase jewellery for personal use and who are generally less financially resilient than corporate entities.

channel_mix.note: AFFIRMATIVE 100% B2B, not an extraction gap. The issuer classifies itself, in its own words, as a pure wholesale / B2B supplier and prints no B2C line anywhere. Primary statements: 'Our Company is engaged in hand crafted gold jewellery wholesale business and providing customisation services to our clients, leveraging over 3 decades of experience in the jewellery industry, operating as a B2B supplier to both corporate and non-corporate clients' (printed p.212 / PDF p.217); 'We then sell these crafted pieces to our clients which include both Corporate clients and Non-Corporate clients. These Clients subsequently sell the jewellery through their retail showrooms or online channels to their consumers' (printed p.202 / PDF p.207) - the consumer sale belongs to the CLIENT, not to the issuer; and 'Shankesh Jewellers is a B2B company based in Mumbai's Zaveri Bazaar, with a pan-India presence' (printed p.189 / PDF p.194; this sentence is from the commissioned CareEdge Report and is repeated in the peer-comparison chapter, so it is attributed, not the issuer's own words - the issuer's own B2B wording is the p.212 sentence above). b2b_pct = 100.0 is the RHP's OWN printed total, not a derived figure: the customer-type table on printed p.200 (PDF p.205) allocates 100.00% of revenue from operations across two trade-client classes and prints no third row. The RHP's own definitions chapter names this metric 'Corporate vs Non-Corporate Client Mix (%) - Revenue split between large jewellery chains and smaller jewellers' (printed p.13 / PDF p.18), i.e. BOTH classes are jewellery trade buyers and both are B2B; the corporate/non-corporate split is a customer-SIZE split inside the B2B channel, not a B2B-vs-B2C split. b2c_pct is left null rather than 0 because the RHP never prints a zero or any B2C figure: searched 'B2C' (0 hits), 'business-to-consumer' (0), 'direct to consumer' (0), 'directly to consumer' (1 hit, and it describes RETAILERS in the CareEdge industry-value-chain chapter, not the issuer), 'no retail' (0), 'our own retail' (0), 'retail outlet' (2, both industry chapter), 'showroom' (2, both the CLIENTS' showrooms), 'franchise' (15, all in the CareEdge industry chapter). order_book.coverage_note: AFFIRMATIVE NIL - the issuer states it maintains NO order book. This is the issuer's disclosure, not a gap in our extraction. Risk Factor 33, headed 'Our Company operates in a business environment where orders are fulfilled based on customer and seasonal demand' (printed p.39 / PDF p.44), states verbatim: 'As our Company does not maintain a formal order book, our revenue generation is dependent on ongoing customer demand, which may fluctuate and be influenced by external market conditions. In the absence of a guaranteed or long-term order pipeline, there is a risk of lower-than-expected order inflows or delays in customer purchases, which could impact our Company's ability to fulfill production and sales targets.' Consistent with that, the RHP states it has no long-term customer contracts: customers 'may terminate their relationship with us, with or without cause, with no advance notice and without compensation. Consequently, there is no commitment on the part of the customer to continue to place new purchase orders with us and as a result, our sales from period to period may fluctuate significantly' (printed p.30 / PDF p.35). Search terms run over the full 426-page text: 'order book' 1 hit (the nil sentence above), 'orders in hand' 0, 'order in hand' 0, 'unexecuted' 0, 'outstanding order' 0, 'order backlog' 0, 'pending order' 0. 'purchase order' appears 3 times and 'work order' twice, none of them a forward-revenue value: they are the product-specific purchase orders placed WITH job-workers, the customers' no-commitment purchase orders (p.30), the suppliers' equivalent, and the 'BUSINESS PROCESS (JOB WORK ORDERS)' flow chart (printed p.211). Therefore value_lakhs, as_of and unexecuted_pct are null because the issuer states there is nothing to report, NOT because the figure could not be located.

business_ops.seasonality: The RHP discloses seasonality as a distinct risk factor (Risk Factor 15): 'Our income and sales are subject to seasonal fluctuations and lower income in a peak season may have a disproportionate effect on our results of operations.' It states the business is subject to significant seasonal fluctuations affecting sales, income and overall financial performance, and that historically the demand for gold jewellery is driven by cultural events, festivals and wedding seasons which vary through the year. Festivals cited elsewhere in the RHP include Akshaya Tritiya, Navratri/Durga Puja, Gudi Padwa, Gurupushyamrut, Diwali and Dhanteras. The Company states its revenues and operations tend to experience peaks and troughs based on the timing of these events; that seasonal fluctuations also affect inventory management, since a large build-up of inventory ahead of peak periods can leave excess stock while insufficient inventory can cause missed sales; and that seasonality creates cash-flow volatility because off-season months generate lower sales and strain working capital. Risk Factor 33 adds that the Company operates in a business environment where orders are generally received based on customer and seasonal demand, and it plans inventory and estimates sales based on the forecast, demand and requirements for forthcoming festivals and seasons. The rural-demand-post-harvest (September-November) and gold-price observations in the same risk factor are attributed to the commissioned CareEdge Report and are not the issuer's own disclosure. No quarter-wise or month-wise revenue seasonality table is printed.
business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Asset-light, non-integrated wholesale model with no backward manufacturing integration and no forward retail integration. The Company describes itself as a wholesale (B2B) player in hand-crafted gold jewellery that acts as principal contractor, managing design, material sourcing and the finished jewellery making process for its clients. Under the heading 'Capacity' the RHP states: 'The manufacturing process is predominantly outsourced to skilled job workers, commonly referred to as Karigars... Hence, we don't have any in-house manufacturing capacity.' Backward: the Company procures pure gold (995 or 999 purity) from bullion dealers / gold merchants, all BIS-marked with the refiner's bar number on the bar and on the invoice; raw material purchases by type (as printed, % of Total Purchase) were Gold Bar 93.27% / 87.12% / 85.61%, Gold Ornaments 6.63% / 12.80% / 14.30%, Stones nil / 0.00% / 0.09%, Miscellaneous 0.10% / 0.08% / 0.00% for FY 2026 / FY 2025 / FY 2024, with total raw material cost of Rs. 15,009.92 million, Rs. 13,231.06 million and Rs. 9,928.30 million respectively; the RHP states the Company does not enter into long-term agreements with suppliers. Production: 72 jobworkers were associated during Fiscal 2026 (87 in Fiscal 2025, 90 in Fiscal 2024), of whom 66 have executed the Company's prescribed agreements, giving access to multiple Karigars; jobworker attrition was 17.24% (Fiscal 2026), 3.33% (Fiscal 2025) and 1.10% (Fiscal 2024); major jobworker manufacturing units are located in Mumbai, Maharashtra. In-house functions retained are design (3 designers in each of Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024), inventory management, purity/metal-pin testing, finishing, final quality control, labelling and photography, and app/online listing - a nine-step process ending with mixed inventory held at the office for clients visiting in person. Forward: the Company does not operate retail showrooms; its Corporate and Non-Corporate Clients resell through their own retail showrooms or online channels. Its mobile application on Google Play Store and App Store is used to showcase designs to clients and is expressly not meant for sale of products. Operations are focused exclusively on domestic markets within India, with a customer network spanning 21 states and 4 union territories; customer counts were 418 (Fiscal 2026), 457 (Fiscal 2025) and 448 (Fiscal 2024), split into repeat customers of 334 / 291 / 279 and new customers of 84 / 166 / 169. Inventory intensity: inventory was Rs. 2,399.58 million / Rs. 1,615.84 million / Rs. 1,314.26 million (62.06% / 66.28% / 75.48% of current assets) with inventory days of 54 / 42 / 45 and inventory turnover of 6.80 / 8.69 / 8.08 for Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024; working capital facilities were Rs. 1,670.00 million as at March 31, 2026, and the Company intends to utilise Rs. 380.00 million of Net Proceeds towards working capital and Rs. 1,580 million towards repayment of working capital debt. Product returns were Rs. 1,177.56 million / Rs. 733.98 million / Rs. 462.72 million, being 7.22% / 5.23% / 4.36% of revenue from operations for Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024, which the RHP attributes primarily to customer preference-related adjustments rather than quality issues. Headcount: 46 permanent employees as of May 31, 2026 (Executive Directors and KMP 4, Accounts and Finance 4, Administration 16, Sales and Marketing 5, Designing and Client Servicing 11, Quality 6), against 44 / 33 / 31 payroll employees at the end of Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024 with employee attrition of 10.39% / 6% / 0%. Insurance covering the gold inventory includes a Jewellers Block Protector Policy no. 48057391 from Iffco-Tokio General Insurance Company Limited providing coverage up to Rs. 4,762.50 million, valid to October 28, 2026.

governance.kmp_attrition_note: kmp_attrition is [] because ZERO KMP or Senior Management departures are disclosed - an affirmative nil from the issuer, not a routing or extraction gap. (1) The RHP's own heading 'Attrition of Key Managerial Personnel and Senior Management' (printed p.251 / PDF p.256) carries exactly one sentence: 'The attrition of Key Managerial Personnel and Senior Management is not high in our Company as compared to the industry.' No KMP or SM attrition RATE, headcount-by-year or exit count is printed anywhere in the RHP. (2) The completeness-framed changes table immediately above it - 'Changes in Key Managerial Personnel or Senior Management during the last three years ... Except as disclosed below, there are no other changes' (printed p.251 / PDF p.256) - lists three rows, ALL APPOINTMENTS, no exit: Sunil Jain, June 05, 2026, 'Appointment of Chief Strategic Officer'; Shweta Dattatray Ravankar, September 05, 2025, 'Appointment of Company Secretary and Compliance Officer'; Chandrashekhar Koraga Shetty, September 05, 2025, 'Appointment of Chief Financial Officer'. (3) The separate board table 'Changes in our Board during the last three years' (printed pp.236-237 / PDF pp.241-242) likewise lists seven rows that are all appointments or designation changes (Kantilal Kheemraj Jain, Mahavir Kantilal Jain x2, Manoj Kantilal Jain, Nikhil Ramesh Parmar, Sanjay Babulal Jain, Sunita Amit Modak) with no cessation or resignation. Across the whole 426-page RHP, 'resign' appears 7 times and none of them is a KMP, Senior Management or director departure (they are the definition footnote of the employee attrition formula, a generic designer-loss risk factor, ESOP lapse-on-resignation terms, and the gratuity accounting policy); 'cessation'/'ceased' appears 9 times, none as a KMP/SM/board exit. WHOSE ATTRITION THE PRINTED PERCENTAGES DESCRIBE - the RHP DOES print attrition figures, but they are WORKFORCE and JOB-WORKER figures and are NOT KMP attrition; recording them as KMP attrition would be a false claim. (a) Job workers / Karigars (contracted artisans, not employees at all), 'Total number of job workers 72 / 87 / 90' and 'Attrition rate of job workers (in %) 17.24% / 3.33% / 1.10%' for Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024 (printed p.195 / PDF p.200). (b) Pay-roll employees under 'Attrition of Employees' (printed pp.214-215 / PDF pp.219-220): 'Total no. of pay-roll employees 44 / 33 / 31'; 'Attrition rate of our employees (%) 10.39% / 6% / 0%'; 'No. of designers 3 / 3 / 3' with designer attrition 0 / 0 / 0; 'No. of employees in the marketing team 5 / 3 / 4' with marketing attrition 0 / 3% / 0%, all for Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024. The printed method is: 'Attrition rate has been calculated by dividing the total number of permanent employees who resigned during the relevant year/period with the total headcount of the permanent employees at the end of the year'. The issuer attributes the rise to 'a competitive job market and availability of better benefit packages elsewhere in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024'. The department break-up on the same page shows 'Executive Directors and KMP 4' out of a total of 46, so the employee attrition percentages are computed over the whole pay-roll and are not decomposable to the KMP layer. No figure printed in this RHP measures KMP or Senior Management attrition.

The body of the risk factor adds: 'There are instances of errors in our corporate records, in relation to certain corporate actions taken by our Company in the past and there may have been certain procedural non-compliances in the past.' orders_not_placed.note: NOT APPLICABLE - NO CAPEX COMPONENT. The flag is false because there are no equipment orders in this Offer at all, not because orders have been placed. COMMITTED vs QUOTED: this RHP contains NO capital expenditure object, NO machinery or equipment annexure, NO supplier names, NO quotations and NO purchase orders. Zero rupees of the Net Proceeds rest on a firm or definitive third-party supply arrangement, and equally zero rest on vendor quotations - the quotation-versus-firm-order question is moot for this issuer. The document is silent on vendor quotations: the only occurrences of the word 'quotation' in the full RHP refer to stock-exchange listing and official quotation of the Equity Shares. The Company is asset-light, outsourcing production to Karigars through Jobworkers, and discloses no owned manufacturing capacity. OBJECT 1 (Rs 1,580.00 million, debt repayment) is the only object with executed contractual documentation behind it: borrowing arrangements with HDFC Bank (Cash Credit & Overdraft, sanctioned November 17 2020, renewed Sep 25 2025) and Kotak Mahindra Bank (Cash Credit, sanctioned March 21 2018, renewed Mar 28 2025), supported by a certificate dated July 16, 2026 from V J Shah & Co., Statutory Auditors, certifying the utilisation of each loan for the purpose for which it was availed and the amount outstanding as on July 15, 2026, obtained under Clause 9(A)(2)(b) of Part A of Schedule VI of the SEBI ICDR Regulations. It is nonetheless NOT a fixed commitment of amount: both facilities are 'Repayable on demand', the lender-wise 'Amount to be repaid from Net Proceeds' column is printed as a placeholder, the RHP states the exact amount will be finalised prior to the filing of the RHP, and it discloses that the Company may repay, refinance or avail additional borrowings prior to Allotment so the aggregate outstanding may vary. Prepayment may attract charges of 2% of the sanctioned credit facility at each lender; the RHP states in one place that such prepayment charges will be funded from internal accruals and in another that payment of pre-payment penalty or premium shall be made from the Net Proceeds with any excess met from internal accruals - an internal inconsistency in the source document. OBJECT 2 (Rs 380.00 million, incremental working capital) rests entirely on MANAGEMENT ESTIMATES, as is typical for a jeweller: it derives from a Board resolution dated June 08, 2026 approving the expected FY 2026-27 working capital requirement, and from holding-period assumptions the Company states are extrapolated from the FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26 trend (inventory 45 days projected against 45/42/54 actual, trade receivables 25 days projected against 14/21/28 actual, other current assets 0.75% of revenue, trade payables less than 1 day, other current liabilities 0.75% of COGS). The projections and assumptions are certified by the Statutory Auditor via certificate dated June 08, 2026 - a certification of the arithmetic and of the stated basis, NOT a firm commitment of spend and NOT an appraisal. OBJECT 3 (General Corporate Purposes) is undetermined in amount and by definition uncommitted. MEANS OF FINANCE: the RHP states the fund requirements for the Objects are proposed to be met from the Net Proceeds and the Company's internal accruals and existing borrowings, without allocating rupee amounts to each source at the project level; a shortfall would be met by exploring a range of options including utilising internal accruals. MONITORING AGENCY: Acuite Ratings & Research Limited, appointed in compliance with Regulation 41 of the SEBI ICDR Regulations to monitor utilisation of the Gross Proceeds prior to the filing of the Red Herring Prospectus, as the Fresh Issue size exceeds Rs 1,000 million; Monitoring Agency Agreement dated August 04, 2026; the Audit Committee and the Monitoring Agency will monitor utilisation, with quarterly disclosure to the Audit Committee and quarterly deviation statements to the Stock Exchanges. INTERIM USE: pending utilisation, the Net Proceeds may be temporarily deposited with one or more scheduled commercial banks under the Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934, with no lien to be created; the Net Proceeds shall not be used for buying, trading or dealing in equity or equity-linked securities of any listed company. The RHP confirms Net Proceeds will not be routed directly or indirectly to Promoters, Promoter Group or Directors, and will not be used to repay loans availed from Promoters, Promoter Group, Directors or any other Body Corporates. OFS: the Offer includes an Offer for Sale of up to 10,000,000 Equity Shares by the Promoter Selling Shareholders; the RHP expressly states the Company will not receive any proceeds from the Offer for Sale and those proceeds will not form part of the Net Proceeds.

overview.business_model: The Company designs and sells hand-crafted gold jewellery (bangles, bridal sets, chokers, jhumkas, necklaces, mangalsutra, rings, across antique, semi-antique, Calcutta, temple, gheru-polish and yellow/rhodium/rose gold categories) but owns no manufacturing infrastructure. It acts as principal contractor: it manages design, material sourcing and the jewellery-making process, and outsources the actual production to localised Karigars engaged through third-party Jobworkers. Revenue comes from two streams: (i) sale of jewellery in 22-karat and 18-karat, and (ii) custom job-work services where the client supplies bullion plus a design and the Company gets it crafted through Karigars and delivers the finished pieces. cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Asset-light, non-integrated wholesale model with no backward manufacturing integration and no forward retail integration. The Company describes itself as a wholesale (B2B) player in hand-crafted gold jewellery that acts as principal contractor, managing design, material sourcing and the finished jewellery making process for its clients. Under the heading 'Capacity' the RHP states: 'The manufacturing process is predominantly outsourced to skilled job workers, commonly referred to as Karigars... Hence, we don't have any in-house manufacturing capacity.' Backward: the Company procures pure gold (995 or 999 purity) from bullion dealers / gold merchants, all BIS-marked with the refiner's bar number on the bar and on the invoice; raw material purchases by type (as printed, % of Total Purchase) were Gold Bar 93.27% / 87.12% / 85.61%, Gold Ornaments 6.63% / 12.80% / 14.30%, Stones nil / 0.00% / 0.09%, Miscellaneous 0.10% / 0.08% / 0.00% for FY 2026 / FY 2025 / FY 2024, with total raw material cost of Rs. 15,009.92 million, Rs. 13,231.06 million and Rs. 9,928.30 million respectively; the RHP states the Company does not enter into long-term agreements with suppliers. Production: 72 jobworkers were associated during Fiscal 2026 (87 in Fiscal 2025, 90 in Fiscal 2024), of whom 66 have executed the Company's prescribed agreements, giving access to multiple Karigars; jobworker attrition was 17.24% (Fiscal 2026), 3.33% (Fiscal 2025) and 1.10% (Fiscal 2024); major jobworker manufacturing units are located in Mumbai, Maharashtra. In-house functions retained are design (3 designers in each of Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024), inventory management, purity/metal-pin testing, finishing, final quality control, labelling and photography, and app/online listing - a nine-step process ending with mixed inventory held at the office for clients visiting in person. Forward: the Company does not operate retail showrooms; its Corporate and Non-Corporate Clients resell through their own retail showrooms or online channels. Its mobile application on Google Play Store and App Store is used to showcase designs to clients and is expressly not meant for sale of products. Operations are focused exclusively on domestic markets within India, with a customer network spanning 21 states and 4 union territories; customer counts were 418 (Fiscal 2026), 457 (Fiscal 2025) and 448 (Fiscal 2024), split into repeat customers of 334 / 291 / 279 and new customers of 84 / 166 / 169. Inventory intensity: inventory was Rs. 2,399.58 million / Rs. 1,615.84 million / Rs. 1,314.26 million (62.06% / 66.28% / 75.48% of current assets) with inventory days of 54 / 42 / 45 and inventory turnover of 6.80 / 8.69 / 8.08 for Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024; working capital facilities were Rs. 1,670.00 million as at March 31, 2026, and the Company intends to utilise Rs. 380.00 million of Net Proceeds towards working capital and Rs. 1,580 million towards repayment of working capital debt. Product returns were Rs. 1,177.56 million / Rs. 733.98 million / Rs. 462.72 million, being 7.22% / 5.23% / 4.36% of revenue from operations for Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024, which the RHP attributes primarily to customer preference-related adjustments rather than quality issues. Headcount: 46 permanent employees as of May 31, 2026 (Executive Directors and KMP 4, Accounts and Finance 4, Administration 16, Sales and Marketing 5, Designing and Client Servicing 11, Quality 6), against 44 / 33 / 31 payroll employees at the end of Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024 with employee attrition of 10.39% / 6% / 0%. Insurance covering the gold inventory includes a Jewellers Block Protector Policy no. 48057391 from Iffco-Tokio General Insurance Company Limited providing coverage up to Rs. 4,762.50 million, valid to October 28, 2026.

demand_drivers.title: Seasonality (RHP report)
demand_drivers.body: The RHP discloses seasonality as a distinct risk factor (Risk Factor 15): 'Our income and sales are subject to seasonal fluctuations and lower income in a peak season may have a disproportionate effect on our results of operations.' It states the business is subject to significant seasonal fluctuations affecting sales, income and overall financial performance, and that historically the demand for gold jewellery is driven by cultural events, festivals and wedding seasons which vary through the year. Festivals cited elsewhere in the RHP include Akshaya Tritiya, Navratri/Durga Puja, Gudi Padwa, Gurupushyamrut, Diwali and Dhanteras. The Company states its revenues and operations tend to experience peaks and troughs based on the timing of these events; that seasonal fluctuations also affect inventory management, since a large build-up of inventory ahead of peak periods can leave excess stock while insufficient inventory can cause missed sales; and that seasonality creates cash-flow volatility because off-season months generate lower sales and strain working capital. Risk Factor 33 adds that the Company operates in a business environment where orders are generally received based on customer and seasonal demand, and it plans inventory and estimates sales based on the forecast, demand and requirements for forthcoming festivals and seasons. The rural-demand-post-harvest (September-November) and gold-price observations in the same risk factor are attributed to the commissioned CareEdge Report and are not the issuer's own disclosure. No quarter-wise or month-wise revenue seasonality table is printed.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Our business and the demand for our product is reliant on the success of our customers’ products with end consumers, and any decline in the demand for the end-products could have an adverse impact on our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.
- Jewellers, particularly smaller players, need to maintain large gold inventories to meet customer demand.
- Our customers, including Corporate Clients, further sell our products to end use customers.
- For further details in relation to our customers, see “Our Business” on page 194.
- Any material downturn in any of our customers services, as a result of increased competition, seasonality of demand, our customers’ failure to successfully market their products or to compete effectively, loss of market share, macroeconomic conditions in the markets of key end-customers, regulatory action, litigation, pricing fluctuation or other factors may impact us.
- Any of these factors could have an adverse effect on the end-use customers and sales of our product could decline substantially which could adversely affect our profitability and result of operations.
- Additionally, the prices of gold and diamonds at a particular time also affect the decision of our customers to purchase jewellery.
- Most of our end-customers of our customers are individuals who purchase jewellery for personal use and who are generally less financially resilient than corporate entities.
